thread:
Aisha Khan: Heads up @diego @nina — MetricWave sent a renewal quote but bumped the ingest unit price and removed volume tiers. Our Feb invoice (MW-INV-4498) is ~2.7x forecast due to an unexpected spike. Can procurement ask for an interim credit and a transition path to a committed model?

Diego Marquez: Oof. Can we confirm spike source first? If it's internal (experiment/bug) they should be more flexible. If it's organic growth, harder to argue.

Nina Rao: Finance pulled the invoice. Quick summary: 
```
api_requests: 4,200,000 @ $0.00015 => $630.00
ingested_tokens: 120,000,000 @ $0.000025 => $3,000.00
storage_snapshot_fee: $150.00
adjustments: -$200.00
INVOICE TOTAL: $3,580.00
```
Note: their meter shows a "burst protection" fee we don't have in our contract. Need a line-by-line with meter IDs and GL codes.

Elliot Brooks: Engineering: Feb burst matches a scheduled load test that wasn't flagged to vendors. We ran a stress-run for latency baselining; that should be excluded per our fair-use clause. I'll pull the test window and logs.

Aisha Khan: Proposed asks to MetricWave: 1) remove/credit the burst fees tied to vendor-exposed tests, 2) provide itemized meter logs + ingestion hashes for disputed ranges, 3) offer a 90-day blended committed-rate option to stabilize next quarters, 4) provide a short-term "bridge" credit to cover the unexpected delta. If they won't budge, start a parallel RFx.

Procure-bot: Reminder: Contract MW-2025-STD renews in 38 days. Recommended: open renewal workflow and attach disputed invoice evidence.

Diego Marquez: @Aisha can you ask them for sample 3/12-month TCO at both on-demand and committed tiers? We'll use that vs LoadBench and QuotaFlow numbers.

Nina Rao: Finance pre-approval: we can accept vendor goodwill credits up to $8k without exec signoff. Anything >20% off list or multi-quarter revenue commits need FP&A + legal review.

Maya Li: Legal: If there's a fair-use clause we can request exclusion for the scheduled load test. I can draft the dispute language. Also recommend asking for a short addendum to avoid similar charges during vendor-approved tests.

Diego Marquez: I'll collect LoadBench and QuotaFlow ballpark pricing by EOD Friday and post a quick matrix. If MetricWave refuses to negotiate, we can start a 30-day alternative evaluation but tag product for potential migration costs.

Aisha Khan: Drafting email to MetricWave now. Will post before sending. Short snippet: 
```
Subject: MW-INV-4498 / renewal MW-2025-STD — request for itemization & credit
Body: Hi Lena, thanks for the renewal. Before we finalize, can you provide detailed metering logs for MW-INV-4498, remove charges associated with our vendor-run load test, and consider a short-term blended-rate or bridge credit to smooth the Q1 impact? Happy to share our logs to help reconcile.
```

Elliot Brooks: Posting the test window and IDs here in 10m.

Nina Rao: Thanks — once we have vendor meter logs we can reconcile and approve pursuing credits. If MetricWave asks for a formal dispute, Finance has the GL evidence ready.

Maya Li: I'll queue a contract addendum template for negotiated credits and testing exclusions.

Aisha Khan: Great. We'll try one round of negotiation with MetricWave, then decide on RFx if unresolved. I'll loop in product & infra if migration risk rises.
